Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg

Class Component3D

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.SceneGraphObject
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.Node
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.Group
org.jdesktop.lg3d.sg.BranchGroup
org.jdesktop.lg3d.wg.Component3D
All Implemented Interfaces:
LgEventSource
Direct Known Subclasses:
Container3D, CornerLogo, Cursor3D, Frame3DWindowDecoration, Java3DGraph, ModelLoader, NativePopupLookAndFeel, NativeWindowLookAndFeel, PopupText, Pseudo3DIcon, RunDialog3D, SnapPreview3D, SprungComponent3D, SwichablePseudo3DIcon, SwingNode, Thumbnail, WindowCarousel3D, WindowSwitcher3D, WorkspacePager3D
public class Component3D extends BranchGroup implements LgEventSource
Component3D object is a top level object for widget development. It supports visual rendering by adding scene graph node children and event handling.

    • Component3D

      public Component3D()
      Creates a new instance of Component3D. By default, it is visible (i.e. isVisible() returns 'ture') and it doesn't have any asscociated cursor.

    • postEvent

      public void postEvent(LgEvent event)
      Post an event into the system with this Component3D object as the source of the event. Note events are only delivered to nodes which are live.
      Specified by:
      postEvent in interface LgEventSource
      Parameters:
      event - the event to post

    • isMouseEventSource

      public boolean isMouseEventSource(Class eventClass)
      If true this component can generate mouse events When a mouse event is captured by the system it searches the scene graph path for the first Component3D that can generate the event. The event is then posted with the component3D as the source. The eventClass argument specifies the kind of mouse event to check if this component is sensitive for.

    • setMouseEventSource

      public void setMouseEventSource(Class eventClass, boolean enabled)
      If true this component can generate mouse events This method should never be called directly by users, instead use setMouseEventSource in Component3D When a mouse event is captured by the system it searches the scene graph path for the first Component3D that can generate the event. The event is then posted with the component3D as the source. The eventClass argument specifies the kind of mouse event this component is sensitive for.

    • setAnimation

      public void setAnimation(Component3DAnimation animation)
      Set the Component3D animation, this controls the 'look and feel' of position, rotation and scale changes for this component. If an animation is already present it will be disabled and the new animation set in it's place. The previous animation is stopped dead and it's final values are NOT copied to the new animation.
